newsitem.title: FINLAND: STORA BUY TALK IMAGINATIVE - UPM .
newsitem.headline: STORA BUY TALK IMAGINATIVE - UPM .

text.p: Finnish forest industry group UPM-Kymmene Oy said on Thursday reports that it may buy Swedish Investor Ab's stake in Swedish forestry group Stora were imaginative.
"It looks like people have a lot of imagination," UPM-Kymmene's chief financial officer Jan-Henrik Kulp told Reuters by telephone.

"I have no knowledge whatsoever about this," Kulp said. He was commenting on Swedish press reports that UPM was looking to use cash gained on the sale of shares in telecoms group Nokia to buy Investor's Stora holding.

"It looks like people already know what to do with the money... and are ready to give us advice," Kulp said, referring to a report in Swedish business newspaper Dagens Industri suggesting UPM had designs on Investor's Stora stake.
The Swedish Wallenberg family's holding company Investor is the single biggest owner of Stora, with 16 percent of votes and 19 percent of the votes in mid-April.

Asked if he denied UPM-Kymmene planned to buy Stora shares with the proceeds from the sale, Kulp said: "This is something that has come from the outside world, and I have no idea what this is all about."

Kulp added that UPM sold only A-series Nokia shares, and said the deal cut its voting rights in Nokia to an estimated six percent from about 10 percent -- assuming no other large owners had made major conversions between A and K shares recently.
But Kulp stressed that this was an estimate, and no one at Nokia was available to comment on the transaction or the figures.
